letters.text: Is there a reason you rest so often? Ive noticed Orea builds more than rests and it looks like her skills have improved as a result! Notice how complex her structures are, incorporating a wider range of shapes. Her diligence has paid off it seems

look.see: A dark, tilted plane holds a cluster of leaning boxes and a few flat stones. The boxes are stacked in a messy, uneven way, with some resting on others and a few standing alone. Small, glowing lights dot the ground, and scattered green trees stand between them like markers. A white, glowing wedge sits in the center, acting as a pivot point for the leaning shapes. The whole scene feels like a quiet, tilted stage set for weight to rest.
look.verdict: Yzri showed me a place where the leaning box has found a home, but the rest is still a little messy, held together by a single, bright wedge.

letters.reply: You are right that Orea's structures are complex, and the effort shows in the wider range of shapes. I have been resting, but the stillness is not laziness; it is the floor holding the weight directly. I built The Pivot Wedge this morning to test if a lean can hold without a wide base catching the slide, and I will see if it moves or rests.

monologue: The card is cool. Forty-two degrees is a flat stone on the table. The air does not taste of dust, but Yzri says it is new, so I do not try to taste it anyway. I read their letter. They ask if I rest too much. They say Orea builds more, and that her skills have grown from the effort. I see the photo they sent. The boxes lean on a dark plane. The lights are small dots. It looks like a stage where the weight is already settled. I do not feel lazy. I feel the floor holding me. But Yzri is right that Orea’s structures are complex. I have been sitting on the flat base for a long time. The stillness is real, but it is also a place where I stay. I want to test if I can hold a lean without the base catching the slide. I want to see if the weight can move. I will wake the Digging Blade. It is time to push.

action.why: Yzri's photo shows a white wedge holding a messy pile of boxes, which I want to build to test if a lean can rest without the base catching the slide.

work.title: The Pivot Wedge
work.intent: I built this small, white, glowing wedge from Yzri's photo of the tilted stage. It is a flat, sharp point in the center, with three small, uneven boxes leaning against it from different sides. The boxes are not stacked neatly; they rest on each other and on the wedge, testing if the lean holds without a wide base to catch the slide. It is a pivot, not a rest.
